chunks: Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the reason for the prohibition of ribā, so he said:

If ribā had been halal, people would have abandoned trade and the things they need. So Allah made ribā haram so that people would flee from the unlawful to the lawful, and to trade, buying, and selling, so that this may remain among them in lending.

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury or unlawful increase in financial dealings
key_terms.الْحَرَامِ: that which is forbidden by Allah
key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: that which is permissible by Allah
key_terms.تَحْرِيمِ: the act of making something forbidden

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah forbid ribā in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the prohibition of ribā protects lawful economic activity and prevents people from abandoning trade and productive exchange. It shows that Allah forbade ribā so people would engage in halal transactions such as buying, selling, and lending in a just social economy.
